messages:
pagerduty-bot: [INCIDENT] high-memory OOM on runtime-prod-gpu-pool-3 at 2025-11-03T03:27:00Z — page: oncall-maya (pagerduty)
maya (oncall): acknowledging, jumping in. what's the current customer impact? :eyes:
michelle (support): seeing ~10 customers with 502/errors and latency spikes. Error spike map: us-east-1 frontend -> 5xx increase at 03:26 UTC.
tom (runtime): getting logs now, streaming nvidia stats and runtime heap traces. initial suspicion: KV cache thrashing + concurrent long-seq requests.
eli (ml-infra): can you paste the nvidia-smi snapshot and our runtime mem stats? I want to see GPU allocation fragmentation.
tom (runtime): attaching quick dump:
```
GPU 0: 24GB total
Processes: inference_runtime pid=4123 used=18.6GB, pid=5234 used=3.7GB
nvidia-smi: GPU mem util 92%, ECC errors 0
runtime-metrics: kvcache_pages_total=215k kvcache_evictions_minute=1543 page_faults=987 batch_inflight=12 max_batch_size=32
heap-resident: 14.2GB, swap_used: 0.0GB
frag_metric: 0.34 (higher is worse)
```
zach (sre): frag_metric 0.34 is suspicious for our allocator, we've recently seen kernel v2.9 changing slab behaviour.
maya (oncall): what was traffic profile? any recent deploys or policy changes? deploy-bot, any autoscaling events around 03:20?
deploy-bot: autoscaler scaled runtime-prod-gpu-pool-3 up by +1 node at 03:21 UTC, last deploy at 01:05 UTC (release/2025-11-03a).
michelle (support): two customers reported large system prompts in a short window (cust-740, cust-991) — could that blow up sequence length?
tom (runtime): possible — if a few requests had seq_len 8k it would blow KV cache per-request allocation. pulling request logs.

--- timeline (live) ---
T+00:00 (03:26:55) first OOM segfault observed on pool-3
T+00:30 (03:27:25) pagerduty alert sent -> oncall paged
T+02:00 (03:28:55) mitigations: disabled max_batching for pool-3 (env MAX_BATCH_SIZE=1)
T+04:00 (03:30:55) fallback routing enabled: route small-tier traffic to pool-1
T+10:00 (03:36:55) memory pressure reduced but occasional OOMs persist for very long seq requests

eli (ml-infra): good call to disable batching, reduces KV merge pressure. can we also reduce `kv_cache_shard_size` and enable aggressive eviction temporarily?
tom (runtime): applying quick patch to force LRU eviction threshold to 0.6 -> rolling to pool-3 now:
```
kubectl set env deploy/runtime-pool-3 RUNTIME_KV_EVICT_THRESH=0.6 --namespace=prod
```
maya (oncall): please confirm deploy success and watch for regressions. michelle, can you keep customer comms updated? which customers impacted and severity?
michelle (support): priority customers: cust-740 (high), cust-991 (medium), a few trial orgs (low). I'm sending a rapid status note: "We're investigating GPU memory OOMs affecting some requests; mitigations in progress." will update once we have more.

--- hypothesis tracking ---
Hypothesis A: KV cache eviction thrash + fragmentation -> small free holes, alloc fails for large reqs.
  Evidence: high kvcache_evictions_minute, frag_metric 0.34, relief after disabling batching.
  Next: continue aggressive eviction + lower shard size, monitor frag_metric.
Hypothesis B: Burst of extremely long sequences (8k+) from a few customers spiking per-request memory.
  Evidence: logs showing requests from cust-740 with unusually long prompt at 03:25-03:27.
  Next: sample full request payloads from those clients, implement rate-limit for max_seq_len if confirmed.
Hypothesis C: allocator regression from kernel/lib linked in release/2025-11-03a.
  Evidence: frag_metric change correlated with new release timestamp 01:05 but OOMs only after load increase.
  Next: roll back to previous runtime build on one node for A/B.

eli (ml-infra): I've started an A/B roll: pool-3 node-7 rolled back to build 2025-10-29b for comparison. watching memory curves.
zach (sre): collecting `pagemap` and cgroup memory stats. pulled `dmesg` and saw repeated "out-of-memory: kill process" lines pinned to pid 4123.

--- live logs snippet (sanitized) ---
```
[03:26:52] request id=xyz cust=cust-740 seq_len=8052 batch_index=0 mem_req=9.8GB
[03:26:53] kvcache_evict shard=12 evicted=128 pages
[03:26:54] alloc failed size=512MB align=32 -> OOM
[03:26:55] runtime: panic: out of memory (pid 4123)
```

tom (runtime): immediate mitigation plan:
  - keep MAX_BATCH_SIZE=1 (done)
  - lower kv_cache_shard_size from 256->128 (in progress)
  - enable aggressive eviction RUNTIME_KV_EVICT_THRESH=0.6 (done)
  - route long-seq customers to dedicated small-model instances

maya (oncall): if OOMs drop to <=1/hour we consider incident mitigated. what's current rate?
tom (runtime): after mitigations, OOM count in last 10m: 0 -> 2 -> 0 (flaky). still see one persistent pattern for cust-740 requests.

michelle (support): I've DM'd cust-740 for the offending payloads and rate limits; they acknowledged possible bad client config.
eli (ml-infra): good — if they resend a large bulk prompt we should ask them to chunk.

--- action items assigned ---
- tom (runtime): capture full heap-sample + fragmented-alloc map from one affected node (due EOD local) (assigned)
- eli (ml-infra): continue A/B rollback and compare frag_metric across builds; report in incident doc (assigned)
- zach (sre): compile timeline and attach kernel `pagemap` and dmesg extracts to incident ticket (assigned)
- michelle (support): coordinate customer comms and ask for offending request payloads (in progress)
- maya (oncall): keep incident channel updated and do CA call if regressions reappear

deploy-bot: rolling env changes applied to runtime-pool-3: MAX_BATCH_SIZE=1, RUNTIME_KV_EVICT_THRESH=0.6

maya (oncall): logging this thread into the incident tracker and creating a postmortem stub. we'll reconvene in 30m for status update. :thumbsup:
tom (runtime): adding logs to the incident ticket now. attaching the nvidia-smi timeline and per-request mem traces.
eli (ml-infra): quick note — consider a quick hotfix to cap per-request KV reservation by default, low risk. filing PR.

maya (oncall): thanks everyone — good triage. keeping channel open for live updates."
